takes.mechanism: 20 carries, 94 yds (4.7 ypc) in his 3rd game back from a January ACL surgery; 73% snaps, 67% rush attempts, 59% routes in week 10; led all 5 SEA RBs in per-touch efficiency, yards after contact, yards before contact, missed tackles forced and target share; was top-10 in red-zone touches last year; SEA's defense keeps games close, which feeds a 15+ touch starter. Tough playoff schedule acknowledged.

takes.why: Price's week-10 touchdown is noise; Charbonnet holds the lead role.
takes.mechanism: Price had 9 carries, 36 yds and a TD in week 10 and 2.7 ypc the week before, while Charbonnet out-snapped and out-carried him.

takes.why: Start him in week 11 against Arizona, then sell high, because Kenneth Walker's return makes him unstartable.
takes.mechanism: Week 11 vs ARI is a smash spot (Sal projects a top-3/4 RB week, 20+ points), but once Walker is back he becomes a 'bust' with no standalone role.

takes.why: Buy Tyson now as a top-20 rest-of-season WR (WR23 / 51st overall for Sal) before his price rises further.
takes.mechanism: Week 10: 11 catches, 80 yds, 13 targets (39-42% target share, 4th in NFL), 0.42 targets per route run (2nd), 4th in air-yard share, NFL-high 52% motion rate, on only a 72% route share that should climb toward 88%; 55% of snaps from the slot in Kellen Moore's offense.

takes.why: Sell Olave, because Tyson's arrival cuts his target earning.
takes.mechanism: Olave's targets per route run fell to 16% with Tyson on the field over the last two weeks, from 23% without him (about a 30% drop); in week 10 he ran a 91% route share but had no target until late in the 3rd quarter.

takes.why: Buy Gordon, because Kyle McCord at QB unlocks a receiving role that could make him a weekly top-12 PPR RB.
takes.mechanism: Week 10: 20 carries, 76 yds, plus 4 catches for 39 yds on 5 targets (3rd on the team) and a season-high 15.2% target share (8th among RBs); about 70% snaps, 80% rush attempts, 51% routes; Malik Willis ranked 49th of 53 QBs in RB target share since 2024; Gordon had 39 and 30 catches in college at Oklahoma State; bye already used; next six: @BUF, NYJ, DEN, CHI, GB, LAC.

takes.why: Buy Downs, who Sal thinks will out-produce Rashee Rice and take Xavier Worthy's routes (65th overall rest of season).
takes.mechanism: First KC game: 4 catches, 53 yds, 1 TD on 5 targets from just 8 routes, versus Worthy's 3 targets on 37 routes and Rice's 6 on 24; routes should climb past 30 per game once he knows the playbook; Mahomes threw two deep TDs at 9.9 YPA that game.

takes.why: Worthy should lose routes to Downs.
takes.mechanism: He drew 3 targets on 37 routes in week 10.

takes.why: Sal expects Downs to out-produce Rice for the rest of the season.
takes.mechanism: He argues Rice is propped up by schemed usage (motion, red zone, slot YAC) while Downs creates on his own; Rice had 6 targets on 24 routes in week 10.

takes.why: Buy Nabers low; he is still a top-15 rest-of-season player for Sal and worth selling Jefferson, Hubbard, Flowers and others to get.
takes.mechanism: His 21% target share vs WAS was his lowest since week 1 and should bounce back to 28-30%+; he had four straight 100-yard games before two quiet ones (5-44 with a fumble in bad weather, 5-43); schedule: JAX, @IND (called arguably the best matchup in football), SF, CLE, DET.

takes.why: Buy Williams from a worried manager; he is a top-10 RB rest of season (21st overall for Sal).
takes.mechanism: 16-63 with no TD in week 10 came from a multi-score trailing script; he already has 10 TDs and 42 red-zone touches (2nd in the NFL); week 10 usage was 71% snaps, 57% routes, 76% rush attempts; Tyler Goodson is on IR, leaving Izzy Abanikanda as his competition; he scored 8 or fewer PPR points in 2 of his last 3 games but 28 the game before.

takes.why: Buy Bears pieces (Burden first in Sal's order) coming out of their bye.
takes.mechanism: CHI has faced one of the hardest schedules so far and now has the 2nd-easiest rest-of-season fantasy schedule; everyone has produced since Caleb Williams returned.

takes.why: Bears buy: Swift.
takes.mechanism: CHI has the 2nd-easiest rest-of-season fantasy schedule after one of the hardest so far.

takes.why: Bears buy: Loveland.
takes.mechanism: CHI has the 2nd-easiest rest-of-season fantasy schedule after one of the hardest so far.

takes.why: Bears buy: Odunze.
takes.mechanism: CHI has the 2nd-easiest rest-of-season fantasy schedule after one of the hardest so far.

takes.why: Bears buy: Caleb Williams.
takes.mechanism: CHI has the 2nd-easiest rest-of-season fantasy schedule after one of the hardest so far.

takes.why: Sal would sell Jefferson to acquire Nabers.
takes.mechanism: This is a relative-value call; he gave no Jefferson-specific evidence.

takes.why: Sell Hubbard off his big game (for example, to get Nabers).
takes.mechanism: This is a sell-high on a spike week; he gave no further numbers.

takes.why: Sal would sell Flowers to get Nabers.
takes.mechanism: This is relative value only.

takes.why: Sal would sell Washington to get Nabers.
takes.mechanism: This is relative value only.

takes.why: Confidence in McMillan is tied to Bryce Young, and they don't trust Young to beat PIT and SEA in the fantasy playoffs.
takes.mechanism: He has been bad for several weeks; the playoff opponents (PIT, SEA) are tough, and they say Young has 'fallen on his face' each time they bought in.

takes.why: Bail on Coker; they would not play him against Baltimore in week 11.
takes.mechanism: Same Bryce Young dependence and tough playoff schedule (PIT, SEA) as McMillan.

takes.why: Pollard could win you a title, and he is a week-11 start of the week against Dallas.
takes.mechanism: He went from 7.9 PPG in weeks 1-6 to 27.4 PPG over the last four weeks after TEN switched from among the slowest paces to fast/no-huddle; playoff schedule is IND, LV, PIT (neutral); week 11 vs DAL has a 55.5 total and a weak DAL run defense.

takes.why: Mike's QB start of the week against SF in Mexico City, though the other hosts called it scary.
takes.mechanism: In his first game back he completed about 70% of his passes for 2 TDs; SF is 30th in schedule-adjusted points allowed to QBs over the last 5 weeks; MIN can't run anyway.

takes.why: Andy's QB start of the week against Arizona.
takes.mechanism: KC are 15.5-point home favorites; ARI's implied total is about 12; in six games as a two-TD favorite Mahomes has averaged 316 yds and 2.7 pass TDs; he was QB5, QB10 and QB1 in recent weeks.

takes.why: Jason's QB start of the week against Tennessee.
takes.mechanism: The total is 55.5; TEN is last in schedule-adjusted points allowed to QBs and now plays at a near-league-fastest pace; Dak threw 5 TDs last week.

takes.why: Mike's RB start of the week against LV, and he feels locked in on Coleman for the rest of the season.
takes.mechanism: Since coming off IR: RB12 and RB6 finishes, 72% snaps, about 19 opportunities per game; R.J. Harvey is still out; DEN are 10-point favorites.

takes.why: Jason's RB start against the Jets, given with heavy self-mocking ('don't listen to me') and a fear of a 33/33/33 split.
takes.mechanism: Harbaugh said Hampton 'reestablished himself' as the lead back; when given about 60% of snaps (twice) he went over 100 rush yds with a TD; last week 4 of 22 carries went 10+ yds and he rushed over expectation on 7 of 8 zone runs; NYJ are 31st in RB rushing yards allowed and last in expected fantasy points allowed to RBs.

takes.why: Andy's WR start of the week against DAL in his return from a shoulder injury; Mike would play him over Tyson.
takes.mechanism: Before the injury: 26% target share and 2.2 yards per route run, one of three rookies since 2021 to hit both (the others were Nabers and Puka Nacua); Calvin Ridley (Wandale) is gone; DAL is 32nd against WRs in a 55.5-total game.

takes.why: Mike's WR start of the week at Chicago, despite the Saints being 11.5-12.5-point underdogs.
takes.mechanism: Targeted on 36% of his routes through two games; led the offense with 11 touches (22.9% of offensive touches, above JSN's season high of 22.6%); CHI is 24th against fantasy WRs since week 5. He has a minor chest injury.

takes.why: Always start Pickens, especially against Tennessee.
takes.mechanism: 3 TDs last week on 51 routes (2nd most of his career); Jerry Jones wants him more involved; TEN is the best matchup for opposing WRs.

takes.why: Mike's TE start (as a MIN stack with Cousins) against SF if he plays; if he is out, play his backup.
takes.mechanism: SF is 30th in schedule-adjusted points allowed to TEs over the last 5 weeks. Hockenson was limited in Wednesday practice.

takes.why: Andy's TE start at Carolina, chasing the Jacoby Brissett effect.
takes.mechanism: 8 targets, 8-82 last week; among 46 QBs with 800+ dropbacks since 2021, Brissett is No. 1 in the share of targets to TEs (about 32%); CAR is 24th in schedule-adjusted points allowed to TEs. Andrews' snaps are still below his early-season level.

takes.why: Jason's TE start against Cincinnati on Monday night in a thin TE week.
takes.mechanism: Averaging 6.5 targets and 5 catches; he was hurt last week and Ben Sinnott filled in; the game has a high total and CIN is bad against TEs.

takes.why: A sneaky start in the DAL-TEN shootout and a waiver option for bye weeks, though Mike prefers Flournoy.
takes.mechanism: 95% of snaps last week; 2nd in the NFL in all-purpose yards; a TD and 71 yds two weeks ago; schemed screen and gadget usage. Xavier Restrepo took slot snaps with Ridley out, and Tate returns.

takes.why: A bye-week waiver start against TEN; Mike prefers him over Dike, but Jason would play Metcalf over him.
takes.mechanism: Top-24 in all but one of his last 6 games and on pace for 1,000+ yds; he is the third target, which makes him risky.

takes.why: You can't play Egbuka right now; Flournoy, Downs and Metcalf are preferred.
takes.mechanism: He is one of three players with 30+ catches and zero forced missed tackles (with 34-year-old Keenan Allen and 33-year-old Tyler Higbee); his output is TD-dependent; TB vs DET has a 43 total.

takes.why: Start Downs over Waddle, Coker or Egbuka.
takes.mechanism: KC's implied total is 28; he played only 17% of snaps in his debut and posted his best fantasy game of the year; Andy Reid praised him after two practices, and his snaps should rise.

takes.why: Play Emmett Johnson against Arizona whether or not Kenneth Walker is active.
takes.mechanism: KC are 15.5-point favorites with heavy play volume and time of possession expected; even garbage-time backup work should produce against ARI.

takes.why: Play Walker if he is active against ARI.
takes.mechanism: He has a sore groin (did not practice Wednesday); the matchup is ARI, with an implied total of about 12, and KC are 15.5-point favorites.

takes.why: Hold McBride and don't trade him; you have to start him even in a bad week 11, and Andy would take McBride over Loveland rest of season.
takes.mechanism: The week-11 projection is about 7-8 catches for 42-50 yds and no TD at KC (ARI implied total about 12, Carson Beck at QB); later matchups are WAS, PHI, bye, NYJ, NO, LV; no waiver TE is better.

takes.why: Ward is a streamable QB against Dallas.
takes.mechanism: DAL is worst against QBs in fantasy points allowed; the game total is 55.5 with both teams playing fast.

takes.why: Start Williams in the TEN shootout, though they called the 95.5 rush+rec yds prop aggressive.
takes.mechanism: TEN is the worst team against fantasy RBs; the total is 55.5.

takes.why: Be nervous about every Saint except possibly the WRs; no NO RB is playable.
takes.mechanism: They are 11.5-12.5-point underdogs at CHI; the offensive line is struggling (starting C and RT missed Wednesday practice); since Kellen Moore took over, NO has trailed on 74% of plays, the highest rate of any employed play-caller.

takes.why: Olave remains a solid play, but watch whether Tyson takes the slot.
takes.mechanism: He has one WR1 week since week 2 but only one week below WR2; the slot is historically central in Kellen Moore's offense, so a second Tyson-led week with the slot snaps would raise concern. Playoff matchups are TB, ARI, ATL.

takes.why: Easy start against Miami.
takes.mechanism: BUF are 16.5-point favorites with an implied total of 31; Allen has never lost at home to MIA, and BUF averages 37 points in those games.

takes.why: Start Cook; the game script favors him late.
takes.mechanism: BUF are 16.5-point favorites against MIA, and they don't expect a shootout.

takes.why: Start Moore against Miami.
takes.mechanism: BUF's implied total is 31.

takes.why: Gordon is the simple Miami start at Buffalo.
takes.mechanism: He is the clear MIA RB in a game where MIA are 16.5-point underdogs.

takes.why: Andy calls Douglas a fine play at BUF, Mike is wary, and both prefer Odunze.
takes.mechanism: Back-to-back 8-target games (8 targets, 71 yds with McCord last week); Buffalo's defense has been better over the last 3 weeks; he was limited in practice.

takes.why: Play Caleb Williams against New Orleans.
takes.mechanism: CHI's implied total is about 30, with a 48.5 total.

takes.why: Start Swift against NO.
takes.mechanism: CHI are 11.5-12.5-point favorites with an implied total of about 30.

takes.why: Monangai is a fine flex-level play in his return against NO.
takes.mechanism: CHI's implied total is 30, and he looked good before.

takes.why: Keep starting Burden ('stay in the flames').
takes.mechanism: He is on a hot streak, and CHI's implied total is about 30.

takes.why: Start Odunze over Caleb Douglas.
takes.mechanism: He has the higher implied total, the better QB and the better situation.

takes.why: Start Loveland this week, though Andy would still take McBride rest of season.
takes.mechanism: He has two bad fantasy-playoff matchups out of three.

takes.why: Baker Mayfield trending toward playing supports Irving (and Gainwell) through the passing game.
takes.mechanism: Mayfield is back at practice; DET has allowed the fewest points per game over the last 5 weeks, and the total is 43.

takes.why: Go 'right back to the well' with Warren at PHI.
takes.mechanism: PIT are 4.5-point road favorites with an implied total of about 21 (total 37.5); PHI is on its third-string QB.

takes.why: Jason's 'disgusto start of the week': he would play Metcalf over DeVonta Smith, Egbuka and Flournoy.
takes.mechanism: PIT is talking about getting him more involved; PHI has been beaten up by WRs despite a good secondary and pass rush. Pittman and Roman Wilson returning from IR dilute the targets.

takes.why: Play Smith if he is active, despite Joe Milton at QB.
takes.mechanism: Smith said he feels '100% now'; PHI's implied total is only 16.5.

takes.why: Lemon is a fine PPR start (WR40, in the Shakir/Sutton range) with limited upside.
takes.mechanism: 6+ catches in three straight games (7-67, 6-57, 6-61), on a 1,000-yd / 100-catch pace over the last 3 weeks; a first-round rookie coming out of his bye. His targets are low-value, and PHI has a third-string QB.

takes.why: Andy would put Barkley back in his lineup.
takes.mechanism: This is a volume RB despite PHI's QB situation; they cited no numbers.

takes.why: Sal ranks Josh Downs above Egbuka rest of season, even after Egbuka's touchdown.
takes.mechanism: This is a relative ranking only.

takes.why: Mike traded for the Cleveland defense specifically for the fantasy playoffs.
takes.mechanism: Their Playoff Primer flagged CLE's playoff-week situation as favorable; Mike made the trade before it aired.

takes.why: Jason picked up the Bears defense to 'smoke' the Saints.
takes.mechanism: CHI are 11.5-12.5-point favorites; Jeffrey Simmons has the defense rolling; NO's offensive line is banged up.

takes.why: Jason dropped the 49ers defense for its matchup against Minnesota.
takes.mechanism: Kirk Cousins and the Vikings are playing well; he doesn't want to mess with it.

takes.why: Sell Deebo off his 26-point week (try for Keenan Allen or Caleb Williams, or package him); Sal ranks him only 101st ROS.
takes.mechanism: Week 10 was 6 touches for 100+ yds and 2 TDs (a 78-yd run) on an 11% target share and 6.2 expected points. Once Mike Evans returns, Deebo is 4th-5th in the pecking order (Evans > Kittle > McCaffrey > Allen/Deebo) on a run-heavy team.

takes.why: Evans is SF's WR1 when he plays; expect him back for the stretch run.
takes.mechanism: Leads the NFL at 4.22 yards per route run; SF rested him for the Vikings/Seahawks games that decide the 1-seed. FF Monday: WR3 of week 11 vs MIN, 'makes things better for San Francisco', and his absence is why Baker/TB collapsed.

takes.why: Sal would rather have Allen than Deebo ROS.
takes.mechanism: He earned a team-high 26% target share in his first SF game, 5 days after the trade.

takes.why: Sell JT on name value now; Sal ranks him 35th ROS and would take Javonte Williams straight up for him.
takes.mechanism: His rush share fell from 74% (wks 1-6) to 49% (wks 7-10) and snaps from 82% to 67% as Seth McGowan took goal-line TDs. Daniel Jones (1.7 QBR in wk 10) and a possible Anthony Richardson switch would kill checkdowns and red-zone rushes. FF Friday: 11-21 in the Thursday loss; Colts 'completely done'.

takes.why: Javonte is a buy target, worth acquiring for Jonathan Taylor straight up.
takes.mechanism: He is not in a split backfield, plays in a top-3 offense with a good line, and gets the red-zone touches. FF Monday: 'inevitable' week to week, and TD-driven in a Cowboys offense scoring 50.

takes.why: Sell Olave; Sal dropped him from about 16th to 30th overall ROS.
takes.mechanism: Rookie Jordyn Tyson took the slot (led NO in slot snaps, 13 targets, 42% TS vs Olave's 13%). Kellen Moore's slot role drives big seasons (Lamb '22, Allen '23, DeVonta), and Olave's 4 best games came from the slot (Andrew Cooper), so a downfield role makes him boom/bust.

takes.why: Tyson's move into the slot is the role that has made Kellen Moore's WRs big fantasy producers.
takes.mechanism: Led NO in slot snaps in week 10: 11-80 on 13 targets (42% TS), 72% routes. NOTE: pre-week-11; FF Monday reports he was soft-benched in week 11.

takes.why: Sell Price (84th ROS) one-for-one for a flex piece such as Jalen Coker, Sam LaPorta, DK Metcalf or Charbonnet.
takes.mechanism: Charbonnet, in his 3rd game back from a torn ACL, took 73% snaps, 67% rushes and 59% routes. Mike Macdonald loves Charbonnet, who will get more explosive as he recovers. Price has fumbling issues and is a backup unless Charbonnet gets hurt.

takes.why: Charbonnet is the Seattle lead back; buy before his workload grows. SEA is on bye in week 12.
takes.mechanism: 73% snaps and 67% rushes in his 3rd game back; top-10 in red-zone touches last year; the ACL recovery trend points up.

takes.why: Unless you are in must-win mode, sell Johnson after his week-11 smash spot, while his trade value peaks.
takes.mechanism: Kenneth Walker (groin) was expected back in week 12 as the workhorse, which would make Johnson unstartable. Suggested returns: Charbonnet, Judkins, KC Concepcion, Egbuka, Josh Downs, Josh Jacobs, Ollie Gordon, or Jayden Daniels if QB-needy.

takes.why: Walker resumes the workhorse role once healthy; Sal calls him an OPOY-type talent.
takes.mechanism: He is nursing a groin injury and KC played it safe as a 15.5-pt favorite. CAUTION: FF Friday heard whispers that he may also miss week 12 (short week vs BUF).

takes.why: Sal names Daniels as a trade return because of his schedule.
takes.mechanism: 'Really nice schedule the next month.' FF counterpoint: he lacks weapons since McLaurin's injury.

takes.why: Bech is worth a real waiver bid: a 2nd-year, 2nd-round WR breaking out with rookie QB Fernando Mendoza.
takes.mechanism: Week 11: 8-88-1 on 9 targets, team-high 26% TS, playing the Bowers role. Mendoza connection; LV has no established WR. Caveat: Bowers (avg 1-2 wk injury per Deepak Chona) likely returns in week 12 and will cut the share. No FAAB % given.

takes.why: Mumpfield is the Rams' WR1 right now and a viable week-12 add (Wednesday at home vs GB).
takes.mechanism: Puka is out for the season, Terrance Ferguson is on IR (hamstring), Davante Adams is not expected until about week 14, and Whittington is on IR. Mumpfield led LAR with a 15% TS in week 10 (3-81) in a 34-6 blowout with only 26 passes. A closer game (LAR -3) means 35+ passes and 5-7 targets; competition is only CJ Daniels and Tutu Atwell.

takes.why: Monitor Rodriguez: he becomes a hot add if Bhayshul Tuten misses practice.
takes.mechanism: Tuten re-hurt the ankle (foot stepped on), finished at 43% snaps and spent time on the exercise bike; Rodriguez took 38%. FF Monday: Tuten left late in week 11 and 'might actually miss time now'. FF Friday: if Tuten is out, start Rodriguez.

takes.why: Add Dike as a rising WR2 behind Carnell Tate, with a 6-8 target-per-game outlook.
takes.mechanism: First game after Wan'Dale Robinson's season-ending IR: team- and season-high 27% TS, 75% routes, played ahead of Ayomanor in 2-WR sets, 6-69 on 7 targets. Profile: about 200 lb with 4.3 speed and a strong 2025 rookie year; Cam Ward is improving and softer matchups lie ahead. FF Sunday (Jason): Dike is available in about 100% of leagues; he named Ja'Kobi Lane and Dike as better options than Germie Bernard or Tre Harris.

takes.why: Mendoza is the best waiver QB for managers who lost Drake Maye, thanks to his playoff schedule.
takes.mechanism: Week 11 at DEN: 267 yds, 7.2 YPA, 3 TD, 1 INT despite 5 sacks. Bowers returns soon. Schedule: home vs LAC in week 12, then TEN and ARI during the fantasy playoffs (FF puts ARI in week 17).

takes.why: Monitor Shipley as Saquon insurance for Thanksgiving vs DAL.
takes.mechanism: Saquon left week 11 with a stinger (he played through one earlier). Per Deepak Chona, most players suit up in week 12 without a dip, even on a short week. Tank Bigsby is on IR, so Shipley is next man up.

takes.why: Sal leaves Hurst on waivers; in deep leagues, spend a couple % of FAAB at most.
takes.mechanism: Week 11: 5-56-2 with a team-high 23% TS and 73% snaps, but still not a top-2 WR in 2-WR sets behind veteran Chris Godwin and Egbuka. Strong profile: 3rd round, Georgia State, 4.42 speed, 28% TS and 1,000 yds in college.

takes.why: Don't add Wallace; start no Cardinal except Trey McBride.
takes.mechanism: Wallace ran 76% routes with a 21% TS (4-57) as the only downfield option, but Josh Johnson managed 155 yds at 5.0 YPA. ARI's WR room is the worst in the league.

takes.why: Wilson is the PIT WR to add, ahead of Max Hurleman, if Germie Bernard is rostered.
takes.mechanism: Back from a hand/wrist injury: 3-43 on 6 targets, 2nd in routes. He has 6+ targets in each of his last 3-4 starts and has chemistry with Rodgers, who hyped him in preseason.

takes.why: Hurleman's week-11 line is noise; DK Metcalf most likely plays in week 12.
takes.mechanism: 6-61-1 on 7 targets, but only on 36% of snaps after Metcalf was ejected. Sal does not expect a Metcalf suspension (FF thinks one is likely).

takes.why: With Jacoby Brissett at QB, Andrews is a strong start.
takes.mechanism: Brissett ranks 1st in TE target % among 46 QBs with 800+ dropbacks since 2021, a tendency that predates Trey McBride. Andrews went 8-8-82 in Brissett's first start. Caution: Josh Cuevas plays a higher snap % than Andrews.

takes.why: Andy's week-11 start of the week, with a 'don't trust me' caveat; Jason preferred Ollie Gordon.
takes.mechanism: 4 of 22 carries went for 10+ yds the prior week; the Jets are 31st in RB rush yds allowed and last in expected FP allowed to RBs; the Chargers said they would feed him. His PrizePicks longest-rush line (14.5) trails only Gibbs, Cook and Warren. Coaching (Keaton Mitchell 'science experiment') is the risk. The Chargers then lost to the Jets.

takes.why: Dynasty: Jason doesn't think Puka plays another down for the Rams (franchise-and-trade is possible), so his 2027 landing spot is uncertain.
takes.mechanism: Puka chose season-ending MCL surgery against the team's advice while he has no extension, after a 3-game personal-conduct suspension (served on IR) and an injury history (core muscle this year, two of four seasons shortened). Andy disagrees on injury-proneness.

takes.why: Watch Adams for the fantasy playoffs; he returns in a couple of weeks as the LAR WR1 with Puka gone.
takes.mechanism: Puka is out for the season and LAR is contending. Sal estimates about week 14 'if that'.

takes.why: Tyson's role is volatile after a soft benching; treat his 13-target week as unreliable.
takes.mechanism: Week 11: 50% snaps, 2 targets, 1-6, a week after 71% snaps and 13 targets. Personnel groupings changed, Kellen Moore's explanation was weak, and Tyson reacts loudly on the field when he isn't targeted. The Saints never led at all in 14 of Moore's 27 games (Jeff Duncan). Pre-game, Jason had started him over DeVonta Smith.

takes.why: Bech is 'not a bank on it'; he is a short-term start only if Bowers is out again.
takes.mechanism: 8-88-1 on 79% snaps vs DEN after 34-40% snaps while returning from injury; 25-26% TS in Mendoza's first two starts. Mike has loved him since the draft. Tre Tucker also drew 10 targets.

takes.why: Mike calls 'bank on it' for Jeanty as a potential playoff hero; Andy and Jason doubt the rushing.
takes.mechanism: Week 11: 11-79 rushing plus 5-90-1 receiving on 84% snaps, and Mendoza's mobility may open lanes. Schedule is good in weeks 14-16 with ARI in week 17; he was the overall RB1 in week 16 last year. Counter: over the prior 6 games he averaged 19.3 rush yds at 3.1 YPC, and the big plays were a wheel-route TD and one long short-yardage run.

takes.why: Roster Hurst but don't start him yet.
takes.mechanism: TB lacks a functioning pass-catcher, and Todd Bowles said they want Hurst more involved coming off the bye. But he had 2 drops and only 1 target total in Baker's 3 previous games back.

takes.why: Don't stream or start Baker even in good matchups (CAR, LAC next).
takes.mechanism: Losing Mike Evans gutted TB's passing game (Egbuka, Hurst and Otton 'nothing'); it is now run game plus checkdowns, with 187 yds in week 11. Jason won't start him until he plays well through injury.

takes.why: Egbuka is 'not it' in year 2.
takes.mechanism: Repeated duds, injuries, and Baker playing hurt; Sal also lists him as a mere trade-return-level asset.

takes.why: Coleman has completed the takeover of the Denver backfield: an every-week start and the OROY favorite.
takes.mechanism: Week 11 was the RB1 overall with 3 TDs; JK Dobbins got 1 carry for 0 yds. 4th-round capital the league undervalued; DEN is 8-2.

takes.why: Hubbard is an every-week dominator: RB2 in week 11 and about RB3 on the season.
takes.mechanism: Jonathan Brooks' 21-day IR window is open, but Brooks was ruled out, so Hubbard keeps the full workload.

takes.why: Irving is the engine of TB's offense.

strategy_notes.note: Off-field/suspension risk to an incumbent is a legitimate accelerant for a rookie's snap timeline [FF]: the day-2/day-3 rookie WR base rate (slow starts, second-half relevance) can be overridden when the player ahead of him is under league investigation or otherwise unlikely to be part of the team's future — the org starts developing the rookie sooner. Check the incumbent's status, not just the rookie's draft capital.

Sanctioned buy conditions for a 30+ receiver [Sal]: he normally avoids aging WRs, but names the exact conjunction that overrides it — (a) the target competition in the room has been vacated, (b) a real QB upgrade arrived, and (c) the ADP has already fallen for the age/injury narrative. All three must hold (A.J. Brown, McLaurin, Evans); efficiency stats that survived the down year (YPRR, first downs per route run, zero drops) are the confirmation that the skills, not the situation, are intact.

Four to six games is the read-the-team threshold [FF]: the hosts converge on refusing to judge a team before week 4 and making the call by weeks 4-6 — early enough to still act before the fantasy playoffs, late enough that schedule strength has evened out. They validate the rule against prior-year week-4 standings (Baltimore 1-3, Arizona 2-2 and never winning again) rather than asserting it.

Price an injury backup against the real starter tiers, not the hype [FF]: when a starter goes down and his backup's ADP spikes, ask where the backup would rank if you KNEW he was starting — put him next to the actual committee starters (Tuten, Price, Warren, Stevenson) and see whether you would take him over any of them. That anchor exposed a pick-37 ADP on a day-3 back with no college production on a low-scoring offense. Pair it with the combine-vs-production check (an A.J. Dillon profile: elite athletic testing that never produced in college).

Do not double- and triple-count a risk that is already in the price [Sal]: for aging or injury-prone veterans, age, injury history and a current camp tightness report are often the same risk restated three ways. Once the ADP has fallen to reflect the known profile, an additional narrative ('everybody on that team gets hurt') is not new information and should not produce a further discount. The test is whether the report changes the week-1 availability branch — 25 days to heal with 'not considered serious' does not.

Stale-ADP trap on news-flip players [FF]: an ADP formed during a player's bad-news window (Nabers' ACL recovery pessimism) is already obsolete the moment the news flips, and every manager in the room is staring at that same number hoping for the steal. Never plan a build around the printed ADP of a player whose situation just improved — assume he goes a full round or more earlier than the number says.

Price a stack by naming the players you pass on [FF]: before drafting a stack partner, pull the platform ADP for that exact pick and say out loud who else is on the board. If the opportunity cost is real (DJ Moore in the late fifth costs Jameson Williams / Luther Burden / Tuten / Price), do not force the stack — either wait for a later round where he is free or switch to a cheaper correlated piece (the late-round TE version of the same stack).

Camp reception counts by quarterback as a target-pecking-order proxy [FF]: they explicitly want, for every team, the full ordered list of how many catches each pass catcher made from the starting QB across training camp — and treat that ordering as real signal while dismissing preseason completion percentage as noise ('they should be failing in preseason'). It is a usage metric available before any snap chart exists, and it resolved their New England pecking order (Brown > Doubs > Stevenson > Douglas > Henry > Boutte).

Three-outcome (wild-card) classification and its roster cap [FF]: sort picks into 'guaranteed to produce on some level' vs wild cards whose range genuinely spans worthless / flex-worthy / league-winning, and deliberately carry only one or two wild cards on a roster — 'you really don't want a bunch of those'. The classification is also a filter for hype: a player who cannot plausibly reach the league-winning end (Bucky Irving with the pass-catching role gone, R.J. Harvey behind two names) does not belong in the bucket regardless of how exciting he is.
Anchor with elite RBs: two RBs in your first three picks (reliability, not breakout swings) — RBs fly early this year and the position is barren by round 5.

The RB dead zone is back — RB24 now costs a 5th-round pick (a 7th in 2024) — grab two elite backs in the first 3-4 rounds and refuse to pay for middling RB2/3s (Etienne, Montgomery, Warren, Pollard all priced above projection).
Elite QB prices are the cheapest in years — Lamar a full round-plus cheaper than last year's QB2; Burrow (rd 5) / Daniels and Hurts (rd 6) are legitimate value even for late-round-QB drafters.
Wait on QB in 1QB: Allen is the lone QB priced in round 2 while Daniels/Hurts/Maye deliver comparable upside ~50 picks later; rounds 10-11 are the last window for Kyler/Mahomes/Purdy types.
Avoid RBs on bad teams: backs on sub-7-win teams hit ADP only ~30% of the time; 2026 teams that are underdogs in 3+ of their first 4 (ARI, CLE, IND, LV, MIA, NYJ, DEN) create uphill starts.
Don't stash day-2/3 rookie WRs early (48%/30% snaps, 2-4 targets through week 6) — only first-round rookies start day one; spend late picks on backup RBs whose value transfers predictably.

The old-WR cliff is the worst bet on the board: the 10 oldest drafted players beat ADP just 30% of the time and old WRs only 21% — this year that's Adams and Evans — with encore-effect exceptions (Henry, Kelce, Stafford).

Tight end is elite-or-punt: pay for Bowers/McBride/Loveland/Warren or wait for late profiles with 17%+ target share and 15%+ air-yard share (Likely, Goedert, Kincaid, Juwan Johnson) — mid-round TEs waste RB/WR upside picks.

Middle-round RB and middle-round TE are the two worst-priced blocks on the 2026 board [FF/Jason] — 'the opportunity cost is too great' there this year. The paired swing: late-round QB has gone so far out of fashion that QBs are falling past their value, so the current edge is the middle-round QB, not the last-round one. Strategy rotates every couple of years as ADP self-corrects; the job is to find whichever block the market has mispriced THIS season, not to re-run last year's rule.

Sleeper-definition inflation [FF]. With ADP now accurate front-to-back and the average manager far more informed, a genuine sleeper can no longer be a known player at a modest discount — it has to be a player where 'right now it seems impossible' and the honest base rate is near-total failure. Corollary they apply on the same breath: late-round shots must go to players you believe are actually GOOD, because 'there are late-round guys who just stink' and opportunity alone on a bad player is a wasted ticket. This is the same bar our league_winners screen enforces.

Dynasty horizon is three years, not ten [FF]. They rejected their own 10-year 'who would you take' question on principle: player trajectories are not forecastable past ~3 years, so dynasty value should be argued on a three-year window. Directly relevant to our never-cut-youth rule — a young stash's thesis should be defensible inside three seasons, not on an indefinite 'someday'.
Never put an early-week (Wed/Thu) player in a FLEX slot; put him in his positional slot so the flex stays open to cover Sunday injuries or news.

Kicker selection: prefer a good kicker on a mediocre offense that settles for 40-60 yard field goals and rarely goes for it on 4th down; avoid kickers on aggressive TD-heavy offenses (DET, LAR, DAL) even if they're better real-life kickers.
Use Vegas player props (reception O/U) as a trustworthy read on a player's expected Week-1 usage; big money keeps those lines tight.
When a team refuses to say where a player's 'soreness' is, read it as PR cover for the previously injured joint (e.g. the knee for a two-time ACL back) — a red flag, not noise.
The days before Week 1 are the peak sell-high window for camp-hype players: benchmark offers against real trades happening in other leagues that week and convert hype into proven target-earners.
Draft capital a team spends to acquire a player reveals its valuation: a 2028 6th-rounder for Kaleb Johnson means RB3, not a real competitor.
Explosive-play seasons regress: 1,000 yards on ~84 targets (18% share) is not repeatable; target share is the sustainable driver (Saquon's 2024-to-2025 as the RB analogue).
A bad offensive line hits inexperienced running backs first; check consensus O-line rankings before buying a new RB1.
Historical base rate: no NFL running back has returned productive from back-to-back ACL tears; lean on the history rather than betting against it.
A QB returning from an Achilles loses downfield power (Cousins, Rodgers precedents), which specifically hurts his deep-threat WR while pushing volume to short-area TE/RB options.
A bottom-5 offense craters even elite-talent pass catchers (ARI 2025 with McBride/Harrison); QB situation can turn a 2nd-round WR into 5th-round value.
New-regime discount: a coaching staff with no draft-capital or money attachment to a player (Skattebo, 4th-round pick) will not force-feed him; check who the new staff signed.
Week 1 for last-round stashes is a usage read, not a points read: track snap share (75%+ = full starter), routes and targets, then either punt them on the first waiver wire or hold with conviction.

Depth-chart order does not predict who takes over after an injury; evaluate the more talented backup (Ollie Gordon over Jaylen Wright, Jonah Coleman over RJ Harvey, Vidal behind Hampton) rather than the listed RB2.

Prefer insurance backs with standalone weekly touches (Corum, Brooks, C-Rod, Monangai, Allgeier, Gainwell) over pure handcuffs; early-season handcuffs with zero standalone value cost you waiver churn.
Only ~24% of top-24 RBs survive 17 weeks — plan on injuries at RB and size handcuff/FAAB accordingly; but don't full-FAAB a backup on a bad offense (Miami) because he won't be a top-10 RB anyway.
Rookie WR base rate: non-high-first-round rookies start slow; only stash the ones projected for 75%+ snaps from Week 1.

TE age curve differs from RB/WR: tight ends are routinely fine at 31-33 (especially TD-dependent ones) without being Hall of Famers; athleticism matters more at TE than any position and TE breakouts often take 4-6 years.
Update conclusions when the data changes (court date moved two months = shorter absence); don't hold a take after its premise moves.
Last-pick IR trick: draft an IR-eligible player (Pacheco, Tyson) with the final pick, move him to IR, and add a free flier — an extra roster spot for nothing.
Week 1 tiebreakers: defenses are ahead of offenses so expect low totals; home favorites get the RB start/sit nod in coin flips; don't overreact to Week 1 results.
Ignore platform Week-1 projections and draft grades: platforms exist to run leagues, not to project players; historically an A grade is a warning and a D/F often means a great team.

Off-field/discipline risk in dynasty: discount a player whose value is team-specific (Rashee Rice) more than one whose skill translates anywhere (Nacua) — the latter gets paid by a WR-needy team even if his current team walks.
Players on the commissioner's exempt list can't go to IR — the stash costs a real bench spot for as long as the case runs.
Thursday is the injury 'swing day': Wednesday DNPs are often veteran rest, while Thursday practice reveals who is actually hurt. Weight Thursday/Friday reports, not Wednesday.

concussion base rate is that only about 40% or fewer of players suit up the week after a concussion; a midweek in-practice soft-tissue exit (e.g. calf) usually means sitting that week, and a strain about 2 games.

decompose an RB's PPG into receiving vs rushing. When more than half comes from receiving and rushing efficiency is bottom-tier, the RB1 price is fragile (red-zone and passing-game usage are the RB 'cheat codes', but they alone don't sustain a top-15 pick).

separate volume quality from volume. A WR's target spike from OT plus repeated screens (screens as an 'extension of the run game') shouldn't be extrapolated, especially when the team is a favorite next week. Check YPRR and aDOT shifts to explain production.

the sell-high discipline is to sell only for proper value measured against a RoS rank list (take anyone ranked above the player 1-for-1), never sell low, and otherwise hold. 'Pickup-and-sell' flips a waiver breakout to managers who valued him more.

trade calculators value assets in a vacuum. Judge deals by starting-lineup impact (does the incoming piece upgrade a weak starter or sit on the bench?). Don't break up one elite player for 2-3 mid starters; use surplus depth to upgrade onesie positions (QB/TE).
play-caller and scheme changes most often happen coming out of a bye, so hold a struggling high-pedigree player through the bye before cutting.

in Thursday decisions with unresolved Sunday injury news (and especially in elimination/death leagues), start the certain Thursday player over a higher-projected player whose availability is uncertain when the projection gap to the fallback is large.
Vegas line and total movement is a real-time injury-intel signal (BAL -3 → CIN -1.5 and total 51.5 → 48.5 priced Lamar's status before official news).

a defense's 'fantasy points allowed' rank can reflect opponent game script and pace, not coverage quality. MIA allows the third-fewest WR points because opponents don't need to pass. Discount WR matchup ranks against slow, bad teams.

designed targets (screens, option routes) are a sticky TE usage metric; a TE with high designed targets and few TDs is a TD-regression buy. In close TE calls, pick the highest TD probability given game environment.

Close-script usage split [Sal]: when a timeshare back's big share came while his team trailed by multiple scores, re-measure the split from the period the game was close (first half / halftime opportunities) and weight it by this week's spread — a favorite will see the close-game split, not the trailing-script one (Warren vs Dowdle).

Return-type ramp rule [Sal]: separate non-injury returns (suspension / exempt list / holdout: in shape, knows the playbook → immediate full role) from injury returns (ACL, PUP: limited, ramping role for 2+ weeks even if practicing in full). Same 'full practice' tag, opposite projections (Jacobs vs Charbonnet).

High-ankle post-return discount [FF]: data show ~3 weeks of below-baseline production AFTER a high-ankle return — keep a dip in the projection for weeks 1-3 back, not just during the absence (refines the low/high ankle rule).

Questionable-WR1 contagion for the QB [FF]: when a QB's top target is active but carrying a soft-tissue tag and WR2 is already out, price the mid-game reaggravation scenario (target tree collapses to a TE) — bench the pocket QB even if the WR is active, while the TE gets a bump (Stafford/Puka/Higbee).

Implied-total tiebreak for RB flex choices [FF]: between two similar RB props, prefer the back on a team implied for 25+ points — rushing-TD odds scale with team total more than yardage lines do (Jacobs vs Woody Marks).
